messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
API name: get information of device connector versions

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends an HTTP GET request to retrieve Device Connector Versions information from a specified URL. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. The URL points to a JSON file containing Device Connector Versions information.

params.description: Optional query parameters to include in the GET request as key-value pairs.

message.content:
Below is a step‑by‑step guide for creating a **RESTful API request** to the *“Get information of device connector versions”* endpoint in **Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1**. The instructions assume you already have a valid user account and that you’re logged into the Dashboard UI. --- ## 1. Locate the API Explorer | Step | Action | |------|--------| | 1 | From the top‑navigation bar, click **Developer** → **API Explorer** (or **API Docs**). | | 2 | In the left‑hand tree, expand **Device Connector** → **GET**. | | 3 | Find the operation named **Get Device Connector Versions** (sometimes listed as `GET /api/v1/device-connector-versions`). | > **Tip:** If you can’t find it, use the search box at the top of the API Explorer and type “device‑connector‑versions”. --- ## 2. Inspect the Endpoint Click the operation to open its details panel. You’ll see: | Item | Description | |------|-------------| | **Path** | `/api/v1/device-connector-versions` | | **Method** | `GET` | | **Parameters** | None (unless you need to filter by `?status=active` etc.) | | **Headers** | `Authorization: Bearer ` (required)
`Accept: application/json` (recommended) | | **Response** | 200 OK – JSON array of connector‑version objects | --- ## 3. Generate the Request ### 3.1 Using the UI “Generate Request” Button 1. **Fill in any optional query parameters** (if the API supports them). 2. Click the **Generate Request** button (usually located at the bottom of the panel). 3. A modal pops up showing the raw request in several formats: * **cURL** * **Python (requests)** * **JavaScript (fetch)** * **Postman Collection** * **Swagger/OpenAPI** snippet 4. Copy the snippet you prefer or click **Copy to Clipboard**. > **Example (cURL)** > ```bash > curl -X GET "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ > -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ > -H "Accept: application/json" > ``` > **Example (Python)** > ```python > import requests > url = "https:///api/v1/device-connector-versions" > headers = { > "Authorization": "Bearer ", > "Accept": "application/json" > } > r = requests.get(url, headers=headers) > print(r.json()) > ``` --- ### 3.2 Using the “Generate Code Snippet” Feature If you prefer a specific language: 1. In the same modal, switch to the **Code Snippet** tab. 2. Choose your language (Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, etc.). 3. Copy the generated code. --- ## 4. Test the Request Inside the Explorer 1. After generating, you can click **Send** (or **Execute**) directly from the modal. 2. The response will appear in the **Response** pane, showing status, headers, and body. 3. Use this to verify that the endpoint works before copying the code. --- ## 5. Authentication – Getting a Bearer Token If you don’t already have a token: ```bash curl -X POST "https:///api/v1/auth/token" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"username":"","password":""}' ``` The response will contain a `token` field. Use that value in the `Authorization` header as shown above. --- ## 6. Quick Reference – Full cURL Example ```bash curl -X GET "https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9..." \ -H "Accept: application/json" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" ``` --- ## 7. Common Pitfalls & Fixes | Issue | Likely Cause | Fix | |-------|--------------|-----| | 401 Unauthorized | Wrong or expired token | Re‑authenticate or refresh token | | 404 Not Found | Wrong path or API version | Verify the path (`/api/v1/...`) and that you’re on Dashboard 6.3.1 | | 400 Bad Request | Unsupported query param | Remove or correct the param | | Response empty | No device connectors exist | Check that connectors are provisioned in the system | --- ## 8. Automating with the `requests_get` Function (Optional) If you’re writing a script in Python and want to use the provided tool: ```python from functions import requests_get url = "https://nexus-dashboard.company.com/api/v1/device-connector-versions" params = {} # add query params if needed response = requests_get({"url": url, "params": params}) print(response) ``` > **Note:** The `requests_get` wrapper automatically handles the GET request; you still need to supply the `Authorization` header manually if the wrapper doesn’t. --- ### Summary 1. Open **API Explorer** → **Device Connector** → **GET** → **Get Device Connector Versions**. 2. Click **Generate Request** → copy the desired snippet. 3. Ensure you have a valid bearer token. 4. Execute the request (via UI or your own code) and verify the JSON response. That’s all you need to generate and test a RESTful request for device connector versions in Cisco Nexus Dashboard 6.3.1. Happy coding!
